newsitem.title: USA: Daewoo CEO has no plans to bid on Russia's Lada.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo CEO has no plans to bid on Russia's Lada.

text.p: Daewoo Group chairman Kim Woo-Choong said on Monday that his company has no plans to make a bid to buy a majority stake in the Russian carmaker Lada.
"We don't have yet any plan for that," Kim told reporters at the Society of Automotive Engineers annual conference here.
General Motors Corp's German unit, Adam Opel AG, confirmed on Monday it would review an offer from Lada's chief that Opel buy a majority stake in Lada.
Opel's comments followed a German newspaper report that quoted Lada chief Vladimir Kadannikov saying he would sell a majority stake to Opel in return for an appropriate investment.

Daewoo outbid GM to buy a controlling stake in Poland's major automaker, FSO, and is bidding against GM to invest in Ukranian automaker AvtoZAZ. But Kim said he does not believe Russia is ready for outside investors to buy into its auto industry.
"We need some more time," he said.
Ukraine is expected to choose between GM and Daewoo for the AvtoZAZ investment by May 1, a government spokesman said on Friday.

An investment tender to find a strategic investor for AvtoZAZ was officially announced earlier this month. Officials say the plant, in the eastern city of Zaporizhya, needs an injection of about $1 billion over the next few years.
AvtoZAZ produced only 6,881 small Tavria and Dana cars last year, compared with 130,000 units in 1992. Its capacity is 150,000 units.
